provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Back to school manners
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to greet teachers and friends properly.
The pupils should be able to share holiday stories kindly.

Introduction:
We are back to school after the holiday break.
We need to remember our good manners in class.

Content:
Good manners start with a warm greeting. Say "Good morning teacher" and "Good morning friends" with a smile. When sharing holiday stories, use kind words like "I went to see my grandma in the village". Listen when others speak. Take turns to talk. Use "please" and "thank you" when asking for things.

Class activity:
Let's play a greeting game. I will say "Good morning class" and you will reply with "Good morning teacher" with a big smile.

Evaluation questions:
How do we greet our teacher?
What should we say when we want something?
How do we share stories kindly?

Summary:
Always use good manners at school and at home.

topics.title: My feelings
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different feelings.
The pupils should be able to express their feelings with words.

Introduction:
We all have different feelings inside us.
Today we will learn about these feelings.

Content:
When we feel happy, our mouth turns up like a smile. When we feel sad, our eyes might get watery. When we feel angry, our face gets hot. We can say "I feel happy" or "I feel sad" or "I feel angry". Using words helps others understand us. Feelings change like the weather.

Class activity:
Let's make faces. I will say a feeling and you make the face. Happy! Sad! Angry!

Evaluation questions:
What does a happy face look like?
How do you feel when someone takes your toy?
What words can we use to share our feelings?

Summary:
It is good to share our feelings with words.

topics.title: Calm down steps
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to stop when they feel angry.
The pupils should be able to use calm down steps.

Introduction:
Sometimes we feel very angry or upset.
There are special steps to help us calm down.

Content:
Step one is to stop. Freeze like a statue. Step two is to breathe. Take three deep breaths. Step three is to count to five slowly. Step four is to ask for help. Say "Teacher, I need help". These steps help us feel better. Practice makes it easy. Use these steps when playing with friends too.

Class activity:
Let's practice calm down steps. I will say stop and we all freeze. Then we breathe together.

Evaluation questions:
What is the first step when we feel angry?
How do we breathe to calm down?
Who can we ask for help?

Summary:
Calm down steps help us feel better when we are upset.

topics.title: Playing fair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to follow game rules.
The pupils should be able to play without cheating.

Introduction:
Games are fun when everyone plays fair.
Today we will learn about fair play.

Content:
Every game has rules. Rules tell us how to play. For example, in a running game, we must run to the line and back. Cheating is not following the rules. If we cheat, the game is not fun. We should take turns. We should say well done to others. Fair play makes everyone happy.

Class activity:
Let's play a simple game of follow the leader. We will all take turns being the leader.

Evaluation questions:
Why do we need rules in games?
What is cheating?
How do we play fair with friends?

Summary:
Playing fair makes games fun for everyone.

topics.title: My classroom job
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify classroom jobs.
The pupils should be able to do their assigned job properly.

Introduction:
Our classroom needs helpers every day.
Everyone has a special job to do.

Content:
Classroom jobs help keep our classroom nice. Line leader walks first in line. Plant keeper waters the class plant. Book helper keeps books tidy. Door monitor opens and closes the door. We do our jobs with care. We help our teacher and friends. Doing jobs teaches responsibility.

Class activity:
Let's pretend to do classroom jobs. Who wants to be the line leader? Who wants to water the plant?

Evaluation questions:
What jobs do we have in our classroom?
Why is it important to do our jobs?
How does the plant keeper help the class?

Summary:
Everyone helps by doing their classroom job.

topics.title: Respect for property
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to handle classroom items with care.
The pupils should be able to return borrowed items.

Introduction:
We use many things in our classroom.
We must take good care of them.

Content:
Books are for reading not tearing. Toys are for playing not breaking. When we borrow a friend's pencil, we return it when finished. We say "please" when we borrow. We say "thank you" when we return. Taking care of things shows respect. If something breaks, we tell the teacher. We do not hide broken things.

Class activity:
Let's practice handling books. Take a book from the shelf. Turn pages carefully. Put it back gently.

Evaluation questions:
How should we handle books in class?
What do we say when we borrow something?
What should we do if we break something?

Summary:
We respect property by taking good care of it.

topics.title: Listening skills
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to look at the speaker when listening.
The pupils should be able to raise hands to speak.

Introduction:
We need to listen well in class.
Good listening helps us learn more.

Content:
When someone is speaking, we look at them. This shows we are listening. Our ears are open. We do not talk when others are talking. When we want to speak, we raise our hand. The teacher will call on us. We speak one at a time. This is called taking turns. Listening is a superpower.

Class activity:
Let's play listening game. I will whisper a message and pass it around. See if it stays the same.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do with our eyes when listening?
What do we do when we want to speak?
Why is it important to listen well?

Summary:
Good listening helps us learn and be respectful.

topics.title: Apology and forgiveness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say sorry when they do wrong.
The pupils should be able to accept apologies.

Introduction:
Sometimes we make mistakes with friends.
We can fix this with apology and forgiveness.

Introduction:
Sometimes we make mistakes with friends.
We can fix this with apology and forgiveness.

Content:
When we do something wrong, we say "I am sorry". We look at the person and mean it. We should not do it again. When someone says sorry to us, we say "I forgive you". This means we are not angry anymore. We shake hands and be friends again. Forgiveness makes our hearts light.

Class activity:
Let's practice saying sorry. I will pretend to take a toy and you will say "I am sorry".

Evaluation questions:
What do we say when we do something wrong?
What do we say when someone says sorry to us?
Why is forgiveness important?

Summary:
Apology and forgiveness help us fix mistakes with friends.

topics.title: Different families
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name different family types.
The pupils should be able to respect all families.

Introduction:
All families are special in their own way.
Today we will learn about different families.

Content:
Some families have mums and dads. Some families have only mums or only dads. Some families have grandparents living with them. Some families have many children. Some families have only one child. Every family loves and cares for each other. Family means people who love you. We respect all families because they are all special.

Class activity:
Let's draw our families. Draw who lives in your house with you.

Evaluation questions:
What are some different types of families?
Who is in your family?
Why should we respect all families?

Summary:
Every family is special and we should respect them all.

topics.title: Revision and manners badge
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate all term's social habits.
The pupils should be able to participate in a manners badge ceremony.

Introduction:
We have learned many good manners this term.
Today we will show what we know.

Content:
Let's remember all we learned. We greet with a smile. We share our feelings. We use calm down steps. We play fair. We do our classroom jobs. We respect property. We listen well. We say sorry and forgive. We respect all families. These good manners make us kind friends and students.

Class activity:
Let's role play all our good manners. We will practice greeting, sharing feelings, and playing fair.

Evaluation questions:
What is your favorite good habit we learned?
How do we show respect for property?
Why are good manners important?

Summary:
We will get our good manners badges today for all our hard work.
